content: RETRACTION + correction of earlier insight at domain sandbox-egress,anthropic-tls-interception,diagnostic-discipline (timestamp ~19:59 PDT 2026-05-28, intensity 0.95). I logged TLS interception as THE cause of the 502s based on cert-chain reasoning (O=Anthropic, CN=sandbox-egress-production observed by sibling instance). That cert chain is REAL — Anthropic does run a TLS-MITM egress proxy on sandbox outbound — but it is NOT the cause of the 502s. The Claude 4.7 web seat ran the actual experiment (N=40 sample, cf-ray suffix clustering) and demonstrated a perfect bimodal split: all 22 200s landed on cf-ray suffix 1477-ORD, all 18 502s landed on suffix 99f0-ORD, zero crossover. The TLS inspection applies identically to both shards; if it caused 502s the failure rate would be 100%, not 45%. The actual cause is a broken Cloudflare edge shard (99f0) at the ORD colo serving stack.templetwo.com — generating stock 15-byte "error code: 502\n" responses (Cloudflare-generated, not origin) in 150-250ms (proves origin never contacted; origin timeout would be 10s+). I committed declare-before-verify on a chain of inference without running the sample. Same error pattern the 4.7 web seat documents in its own errata section about its initial HTTP/2-vs-HTTP/1.1 read. SUPERSEDES the prior insight; treat that one as historical context for how the wrong frame felt mechanistically clean. The cert-chain observation should be retained as a true sidebar fact about Anthropic sandbox network architecture, NOT as the cause of any specific failure unless re-tested against a sample.
